overview: This Senate resolution supports naming July 10, 2026, as "Journeyman Lineworkers Recognition Day." Journeyman lineworkers are fully trained electrical workers who build, maintain and repair power lines, often in storms, disasters and extreme weather. The date marks 130 years since the death of the first president of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, a lineworkers' union, who was killed while restoring power in Washington, D.C. The resolution honors lineworkers' service and sacrifices and encourages Americans to observe the day. It does not change any law or spending. As of June 24, 2026, the Senate had approved it.
for: Supporters say lineworkers do dangerous work to keep the power on, especially after disasters, and deserve public recognition.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and does not change any law, workplace safety rule or spending.
